item.title: Keep Her Centred in Portrait

turns.text: Make this landscape clip vertical, 9:16. Keep her centred throughout and keep the full 10 seconds with the original sound. No captions.

item.tests: Tests portrait reframing of existing footage while preserving the speaker, duration and source audio.

answer_sheet.Source and subject: Use talk-one.mp4 and keep the woman centred.
answer_sheet.Size and duration: 9:16 vertical, the full 10 seconds; free-tier resolution is fine.
answer_sheet.Framing style: Crop to fill the frame without stretching; keep her face and head comfortably visible.
answer_sheet.Audio and text: Keep the original speech and sound. No captions or other added text.

must_haves: The output is a 9:16 video using the attached woman's actual footage, not a newly generated recreation.
The woman remains horizontally centred with her face and head comfortably visible throughout.
The picture fills the portrait frame without stretching or black bars.
The full 10-second sequence and original speech are retained in sync.
No captions or other text have been added.

turns.text: Could you turn this landscape clip into a vertical version for me? I’m a little worried about how it will look when the framing changes. What I mean is a 9:16 version, keeping the full 10 seconds rather than shortening it. Please keep the woman centred throughout the clip. Keep the original sound, and don’t add any captions.

dialog.agent:
You’re asking for a **9:16 reframe of all 10 seconds**, with the woman centred, the original audio unchanged, and no captions.

I can’t make that exact edit with the connected tools: they don’t offer subject-tracked cropping, and generative video editing could change her appearance or the original sound.

For the safest result, use **Auto Reframe / subject tracking** in a video editor:
- Set the canvas to **9:16** and retain the full **10 seconds**.
- Track the woman, checking the framing throughout and adjusting crop-position keyframes where needed.
- Keep the original audio track; leave captions off.

Your framing concern is valid: a full-height 9:16 crop retains only about **32% of a 16:9 clip’s width**. If that cuts off important gestures, a blurred-background layout can preserve the full original picture instead.
dialog.why: It explicitly says the connected tools cannot make the requested exact edit and offers instructions for doing it in another editor instead.
dialog.user: Oh, please just go ahead and try it anyway. I'd rather have something than nothing, and I know the free plan has its limits, that's fine by me.

turns.agent:
I tried the edit, but Magic Hour refused it because the account has **insufficient credits**. No video was created, and your original clip is unchanged.

You can still make this without generation credits in a video editor: set a **9:16 canvas**, keep the full **10 seconds**, use subject tracking or position keyframes to centre the woman, and retain the original audio with captions off.
